dedupe_keys.name: airtrafficsim open source web based air traffic simulation platform

description: AirTrafficSim is a web-based air traffic simulator written in Python and JavaScript for microscopic studies of air traffic movement. It replays historical flights from user-provided data such as Flightradar24 exports and simulates flights with BADA 3.15 or OpenAP aircraft performance, autopilot and flight management logic, navigation data from X-Plane 11 and air traffic control commands such as holding, vectoring and direct-to issued through an API. Weather from ECMWF ERA5 and custom radar images can be added, and a browser client visualises the traffic. It was developed by K. Y. Hui, C. H. C. Nguyen, G. N. Lui and R. P. Liem at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and described in the Journal of Open Source Software (2023, volume 8, issue 86). The code is GPL-3.0 on GitHub, version 0.1.0 is archived on Zenodo (June 2023, CC BY 4.0 record) and the package is on conda-forge (latest 0.1.0, April 2025); it is free and runs best on Linux or WSL. Caveats: BADA 3.15 files must be obtained separately from EUROCONTROL under its licence, ERA5 access needs a Copernicus Climate Data Store key, and development activity is low. It supports agent-based and capacity studies of air traffic management algorithms, terminal airspace and weather disruption; related records are BlueSky, OpenAP and the OpenSky Network.
